messages:
alex: rolling canary 2026-03-15T10:40 UTC -> runtime v2.18.0. seeing a handful of p95 spikes in the canary cohort, filing here to coordinate.

maria: saw same from telemetry, p95 up ~220ms on short requests, p99 tail unchanged. affected cohort: canary-4 (auth-heavy).

tyler: any config changes? kernel selector or scheduling?

alex: only change in this rollout was kernel scheduler tweak + auth cache TTL bump (10s -> 30s) to reduce auth backend calls.

kim: can you paste the graph slice+query? which route?

alex: route: /v1/generate (auth labeled). quick prometheus: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{cohort="canary-4",route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (le))` shows shift from 110ms -> 330ms after 10:37 UTC.

maria: deploy-bot: rollout complete on 4 hosts at 10:36.
deploy-bot: Rollout v2.18.0 -> 4 hosts (canary) succeeded in 00:02:14 :white_check_mark:

tyler: interesting that p99 untouched. suggests extra fixed overhead affecting many requests rather than tail event. maybe auth caching change increased sync waits?

kim: hairball: auth cache TTL increase should reduce auth calls; it shouldn't add latency. could be cache-lock contention + hot-keying for service tokens.

alex: reproduced locally with a small load generator hitting the auth path. when auth cache misses, we see auth backend time ~50ms but when cache hits, still +200ms extra in runtime.

sre-oncall: can you run a focused bisect? rollback one host to v2.17 and diff?

alex: rolling back one of the 4 canary hosts now (host-12).
alex: host-12 rolled back at 10:48 -> now 3 canary hosts on v2.18, 1 on v2.17.

maria: early numbers: p95 for host-12 cohort (v2.17) is 115ms, others ~320ms. rollback seems to remove the regressed latency.
tyler: that points to v2.18 change. can we bisect between kernel-scheduler vs auth-cache TTL? there were two commits.

kim: propose quick A/B: revert TTL only on remaining hosts (set back to 10s) then check. If fixed -> TTL. If not -> scheduler.
alex: applying TTL revert via feature flag to two hosts (host-13, host-14).

alex: feature flag flip done at 10:58.

maria: update: hosts with TTL reverted show p95 near 120ms. hosts still with TTL=30s at ~320ms.
tyler: TTL change is the culprit or at least a major factor. curious why TTL increase adds 200ms per request on hits.

kim: hypothesis: TTL bump changed eviction windows causing more concurrent auth refresh work for high-rps tokens, plus cache locking is serialized. need to check per-token concurrency metrics.
sre-oncall: collect stack traces / blocking syscalls on v2.18 hosts when spike happens. enable verbose auth cache logs (sampling).

alex: enabling verbose sampling (1%) and capturing pprof on one affected host now.

maria: also had billing customer report: increased costs from retries due to client-side timeouts hitting 2xx but slow. flagging CS to avoid churn.

kim: quick mitigation: roll TTL back cluster-wide for canary and halt rollout to remaining stages. also add per-token refresh jitter + switch lock to RW lock to reduce contention in next patch.

tyler: ack. I'll add an emergency change to rollout plan: pause and revert TTL globally, then ship scheduler-only change separately.

alex: doing cluster-wide revert now (10:12).
deploy-bot: FeatureFlag(auth.cache_ttl)=10 -> updated on 24 hosts :white_check_mark:

maria: post-revert metrics: p95 back to baseline ~115ms across canaries. p99 stable.

kim: follow-ups: add unit test for cache hot-key, benchmark lock scenario, and add telemetry for per-token concurrent refreshes + latency contribution. also document rollout doc note to avoid simultaneous TTL + scheduler changes.
tyler: I'll open a small RFC and a postmortem ticket. assign owners?

alex: owners: kim (root cause + patch), tyler (rollout plan + RFC), maria (telemetry + dashboards), me (customer comms).

maria: customer-facing note drafted, notifying affected customers and refunds queued.

sre-oncall: marking incident resolved for now but keep monitoring for 24h.

alex: thanks all. main takeaways: don't bundle cache TTL semantics changes with kernel scheduler tweaks; TTL increases can unexpectedly serialize work on hot keys.

kim: attaching repro snippet for internal playbook:```bash
# repro: single-token hotkey load against canary host
for i in {1..2000}; do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer HOT_TOKEN" "https://canary-host-14.internal/v1/generate" &
done
wait
```

kim: also config to simulate lock contention: auth.cache.lock_type=exclusive vs rw.

alex: saving logs and pprofs to /var/tmp/canary-4976543210 for postmortem.

maria: closing thread, will move postmortem notes to docs repo. :white_check_mark:
